🇺🇸🇮🇷 Oil just fell to $87... but America’s shrinking stockpiles point to $126 a barrel by June

Philip Pilkington, a macroeconomist, built his forecast on one number, which is how much crude and fuel the US has left in storage, including the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. 

Those stockpiles have dropped every month since the war began, and by that measure oil should be near $100 today.

If the drawdowns continue at the same pace, Philip gets $126 by June 2027. 

If releases stop at the reserve’s legal floor it’s $147, and draining it to the physical limit still leaves $130.

The bigger hit lands on Treasuries, where his model puts the 10-year yield at 5.8% to 6.2%, up from about 5% now, a level he says brings a financial crisis. 

He’ll change his call the day inventories stop falling, and so far they haven’t.

🚨🇺🇸 A simple majority of Nvidia's 11 directors can remove Jensen Huang "with or without cause"... and they are reportedly meeting TONIGHT

Reuters says the meeting is under way, three days after the same board said it had confidence in him.

Ten of the eleven directors are independent, and he owns about 3.6% of the stock, which is nowhere near enough to stop a vote against him.

One longtime tech analyst described what the board is weighing:

"Jensen is not replaceable... there is no other person on the management team bench that can step in seamlessly as CEO."

With no successor named, speculation has turned to his children, who both started as interns and now hold senior roles.

His daughter Madison, 35, leads marketing for Nvidia’s robotics and AI platforms and travels with him to major events, while his son Spencer, 36, manages robotics products.

A Huang in charge would signal continuity, but their father said last month either would have to earn the job, and neither is an executive officer, so a temporary chief from outside the family is the likelier first move.

Source: Reuters, WSJ / Writer: Daniel

🚨 This could be the final blow to the AI bubble.

Nvidia is facing its biggest leadership crisis, and the consequences could be devastating for the entire market.

Jensen Huang has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife amid reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly suspects of spying for China.

Now, The New York Times has reported allegations of a SECOND affair with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive who reports directly to him.

And according to The Wall Street Journal, Nvidia's board is considering removing Huang as CEO.

This could become a massive problem for the AI industry.

Jensen Huang took Nvidia from a gaming chipmaker to a company valued at nearly $5 TRILLION.

He has led it for 33 years, and almost every major AI company depends heavily on Nvidia's technology.

Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon and OpenAI have invested enormous amounts in AI infrastructure powered by its chips.

But Nvidia has no clear successor.

If Huang is forced to leave, investors could lose confidence in the company, potentially triggering another massive selloff.

And Nvidia isn't just another stock.

With a market value of roughly $4 TRILLION, a major crash could drag down the Nasdaq, semiconductor companies and other AI stocks.

The timing is extremely concerning.

AI companies are already facing massive debt, expensive valuations and growing questions about whether their enormous spending will generate enough profits.

And Bitcoin could get hit even harder.

If Nvidia's problems trigger a broader stock market crash, investors could sell Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies to reduce risk or cover losses.

That could trigger billions in leveraged liquidations, putting even more pressure on an already struggling crypto market.

The AI boom has become heavily dependent on Nvidia, and Nvidia has become heavily dependent on Jensen Huang.

If the controversies force him out and trigger a broader loss of confidence, this could become the final blow to an AI market already under massive pressure.
